By correlating spectral slope with accretion rate, this work provides new insights into the interplay between accretion physics, jet activity, and the cosmic evolution of quasars.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes 642 quasars (561 radio-quiet, 81 radio-loud) using X-ray (XMM-Newton) and optical (SDSS) data. Radio-quiet quasars show softer X-ray spectra (Γ ≈ 2.0) and higher Eddington ratios (log λ_Edd ≈ -1.2), with a positive Γ–λ_Edd correlation supporting disk–corona models. Accretion trends with redshift and black hole mass are consistent with recent AGN evolution studies.
AI.motivation: To establish and characterize the fundamental relationship between the photon index (Γ) and Eddington ratio (λ_Edd) for radio-quiet quasars, and to understand accretion physics, jet activity, and cosmic evolution of quasars.
AI.method: Cross-matched XMM-Newton Serendipitous Source Catalog (DR11) with SDSS (DR16) quasar catalog; applied stringent quality filtering and automated spectral reduction; derived photon indices and intrinsic X-ray luminosities; classified sources as radio-quiet (561) and radio-loud (81) using multiwavelength data; estimated bolometric luminosities and Eddington ratios from absorption-corrected X-ray measurements and virial black hole masses.
AI.result: Radio-quiet quasars show higher Eddington ratios peaking at log λ_Edd ≈ -1.2, softer spectra (Γ ≈ 2.0), and a statistically significant positive correlation between Γ and λ_Edd. λ_Edd increases with redshift and decreases with black hole mass for RQ quasars, consistent with recent results.
AI.conclusion: The positive Γ–λ_Edd correlation supports disk–corona coupling models. The accretion trends with redshift and black hole mass highlight the universal nature of accretion-driven evolution in quasars, providing new insights into the interplay between accretion physics, jet activity, and cosmic evolution.

title: The $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$R_{\rm b}$ relation and the high-mass end of the $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$σ$ relation
comment: 15 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Using a sample of 151 galaxies with dynamically measured black hole (BH) masses ($M_{\rm BH}$), we investigate the scaling relations between $M_{\rm BH}$ and the stellar velocity dispersion, $σ$, and, for a subsample of 30 core-Sérsic galaxies, between $M_{\rm BH}$ and the size of the partially depleted core, $R_{\rm b}$. Core-Sérsic galaxies, identified using high-resolution $Hubble ~ Space ~ Telescope$ imaging and spanning both the normal-core $(R_{\rm b}<0.5$ kpc) and large-core ($R_{\rm b}>0.5$ kpc) regimes, define an updated $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$R_{\rm b}$ relation of the form $M_{\rm BH} \propto R_{\rm b}^{1.16 \pm 0.10}$, with an rms scatter of $Δ_{\rm rms} \simeq 0.28$ dex in $\log M_{\rm BH}$. We find that Sérsic and normal-core galaxies together follow a common log-linear $M_{\rm BH}$-$σ$ relation with a slope of $4.95 \pm 0.29$ and a scatter $Δ_{\rm rms} \simeq 0.46$ dex. Deviations from this relation arise at the highest BH masses, where large-core galaxies, including six with direct $M_{\rm BH}$ measurements, drive a significant upturn. We find that these galaxies typically host ultramassive black holes whose masses scale more strongly with $R_{\rm b}$ than $σ$, and lie $\sim (1-4$) $~\times$ the intrinsic scatter (0.39 dex) above the relation defined by Sérsic and normal-core galaxies. The $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$R_{\rm b}$ relation shows $\sim 30$-$47\%$ less scatter in $\log M_{\rm BH}$ than the corresponding $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$σ$ relation for the same sample. We interpret the high-mass upturn in the $M_{\rm BH}$$-$$σ$ diagram as a consequence of successive major, dry mergers, a scenario that naturally explains the observed flattening of the $σ-L_V$ relation at $M_V < -23.5$ mag.

AI.tldr: This study uses 151 galaxies to update the scaling relations between black hole mass and stellar velocity dispersion (M_BH-σ) and core size (M_BH-R_b) for core-Sérsic galaxies, finding that ultramassive black holes in large-core galaxies deviate upward from the M_BH-σ relation and show tighter correlation with core size, with the upturn explained by successive major dry mergers.
AI.motivation: To better understand the co-evolution of supermassive black holes and their host galaxies by refining the M_BH-σ and M_BH-R_b scaling relations using a large sample of dynamically measured black hole masses, particularly focusing on core-Sérsic galaxies that host the most massive black holes.
AI.method: Analysis of 151 galaxies with dynamically measured BH masses; classification into Sérsic, normal-core (R_b<0.5 kpc), and large-core (R_b>0.5 kpc) galaxies using HST imaging; fitting log-linear M_BH-σ and M_BH-R_b relations.
AI.result: M_BH-σ relation slope=4.95±0.29, scatter~0.46 dex for Sérsic+normal-core; large-core galaxies show upward deviation hosting ultramassive BHs. M_BH-R_b relation slope=1.16±0.10, scatter~0.28 dex, showing 30-47% less scatter than M_BH-σ.
AI.conclusion: Ultramassive BHs in large-core galaxies scale more strongly with core size than velocity dispersion; the high-mass upturn in M_BH-σ is due to successive major dry mergers, explaining the σ-L_V flattening at high luminosities.

title: Unprecedented Constraints on Gas Flows at High Redshift Using Deep JWST/NIRSpec Observations from the LyC22, EXCELS, and AURORA Surveys
comment: 31 pages, 14 figures, 3 tables, submitted to ApJ
summary: We investigate how low-ionization gas flows in typical star-forming galaxies at $z\sim3$ depend on galaxy intrinsic properties and viewing angle. For this analysis we use JWST/NIRSpec observations of rest-frame near-UV Fe II and Mg II absorption, and rest-frame optical Na D absorption. This study combines galaxies from the LyC22, EXCELS, and AURORA surveys and contains 176, 197, and 315 galaxies, respectively, with Fe II, Mg II, and Na D coverage. Based on both individual and composite spectra, we find no statistically significant correlations between outflow velocity and galaxy properties. However, galaxies with detected outflows tend towards higher stellar masses, SFR, and $Σ_{\rm SFR}$ than those without outflows, suggesting that the two samples are not drawn from the same parent population. Finally, we additionally find that Mg II emission is preferentially detected in galaxies with lower stellar mass and $A_V$, and higher sSFR, consistent with conditions that favor the escape of resonantly scattered line and ionizing continuum radiation. We present the first evidence in $z\sim3$ star-forming galaxies that properties of the absorption lines depend on galaxy inclination, with more face-on systems showing stronger absorption and higher outflow velocities, while inflowing gas is more frequently detected in more highly inclined galaxies. These trends are consistent with observations at $z\lesssim1$ and predictions from cosmological simulations in which galactic winds are launched perpendicular to the galactic disks, while accretion occurs primarily along the disk plane.

AI.tldr: Study of low-ionization gas outflows in z~3 star-forming galaxies using JWST/NIRSpec observations of Fe II, Mg II, and Na D absorption lines, finding no strong correlations between outflow velocity and galaxy properties, but detecting inclination-dependent trends: face-on galaxies show stronger outflows, edge-on galaxies show more inflowing gas.
AI.motivation: To understand how low-ionization gas flows in high-redshift (z~3) star-forming galaxies depend on intrinsic galaxy properties and viewing angle, leveraging JWST/NIRSpec's capability to observe rest-frame UV and optical absorption lines.
AI.method: Analyzed JWST/NIRSpec spectra of Fe II, Mg II, and Na D absorption lines from 176, 197, and 315 galaxies (LyC22, EXCELS, AURORA surveys). Used individual and composite spectra to examine correlations with stellar mass, SFR, Σ_SFR, A_V, sSFR, and galaxy inclination.
AI.result: No statistically significant correlations between outflow velocity and galaxy properties. Galaxies with detected outflows tend toward higher stellar mass, SFR, and Σ_SFR. Mg II emission preferentially detected in lower-mass, lower-A_V, higher-sSFR galaxies. Face-on galaxies show stronger absorption and higher outflow velocities; inflowing gas more common in highly inclined galaxies.
AI.conclusion: First evidence at z~3 that absorption line properties depend on galaxy inclination, consistent with lower-redshift observations and simulations where winds are perpendicular to the disk and accretion occurs along the disk plane.

title: Supermassive Black Hole Assembly from Heavy Seeds with Dynamical Friction in the BRAHMA Simulations: Implications for JWST, LISA, and the Local Universe
summary: The JWST discoveries of supermassive black holes (BHs) at $z \gtrsim 5$ may provide key insights into their seeding origins. Using new $[18{-}72~\rm Mpc]^3$ BRAHMA cosmological simulations, we investigate how variations in heavy-seed prescriptions, coupled with a subgrid dynamical friction model, shape BH populations at $z \sim 5$ and $z \sim 0$. We consider two "lenient'' seed models, in which all halos containing sufficient dense & metal-poor gas form $\sim10^4$ and $\sim10^5~M_{\odot}$ seeds, and a "strict'' seed model, in which $\sim10^5 M_{\odot}$ seeds form only under additional constraints motivated by direct collapse black hole formation. By $z \sim 5$, all models produce $M_*-M_{\rm BH}$ relations broadly consistent with the observed local Universe for $M_*\gtrsim10^9~M_{\odot}$ galaxies, but only the lenient scenarios generate systems near the upper envelope of the observed local scatter. In galaxies hosting $M_{\rm BH} \sim 10^8$-$10^9~M_{\odot}$ BHs, lenient production of $\sim10^5~M_{\odot}$ seeds also produces multiple overmassive systems with $M_{\rm BH}/M_* \gtrsim 0.01$. Although their growth is dominated by seeding and mergers, these systems reach luminosities of $\sim10^{43}$-$10^{45}\mathrm{erg s^{-1}}$, comparable to those inferred for JWST-detected BHs. As a key observational signature, the lenient seed models yield merger rates of $\gtrsim100\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ and near-unity local BH occupation fractions even in galaxies with $M_* \lesssim 10^7~M_{\odot}$. In contrast, the strict seed model produces merger rates of only $\sim1\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ and local occupation fractions of $\lesssim10\%$ for galaxies with $M_* \lesssim 10^8~M_{\odot}$. Future gravitational-wave event rates and measurements of local BH occupation fractions will therefore provide strong constraints on the dominant pathways responsible for high-redshift BH assembly.

AI.tldr: Using BRAHMA cosmological simulations, this paper shows that different heavy-seed prescriptions for supermassive black hole formation at high redshift (z≥5) produce distinct observational signatures at z~0. Lenient seed models generate abundant overmassive BHs matching JWST detections and high merger rates (~100/yr) with near-unity occupation fractions in dwarf galaxies, while strict seed models yield low merger rates (~1/yr) and sparse occupation (~10% in low-mass galaxies).
AI.motivation: JWST discoveries of supermassive BHs at z≥5 provide potential insights into BH seeding origins, motivating investigation of how different heavy-seed prescriptions affect BH populations across cosmic time.
AI.method: Using BRAHMA cosmological simulations ([18-72 Mpc]^3 volumes) with a subgrid dynamical friction model, the authors compare lenient seed models (all halos with dense metal-poor gas form ~10^4 or ~10^5 M⊙ seeds) and a strict seed model (~10^5 M⊙ seeds only under direct collapse BH formation constraints).
AI.result: All models produce M*-M_BH relations consistent with local Universe for M*≳10^9 M⊙ galaxies by z~5, but only lenient scenarios generate systems at the upper envelope of observed scatter. Lenient ~10^5 M⊙ seeds produce multiple overmassive systems (M_BH/M* ≳ 0.01) with luminosities ~10^43-10^45 erg/s matching JWST-detected BHs. Lenient models yield merger rates >100/yr and near-unity BH occupation fractions even in M*≲10^7 M⊙ galaxies, while strict models yield ~1/yr merger rates and <10% occupation for M*≲10^8 M⊙ galaxies.
AI.conclusion: Future gravitational-wave event rates and local BH occupation fraction measurements will strongly constrain the dominant high-redshift BH assembly pathways.

title: SIDM and CDM interpretations of the million-solar-mass lensing perturber JVAS B1938+666-$\mathcal{V}$
summary: A $10^6\,M_\odot$ object has recently been inferred from gravitational imaging of the strong-lensing system JVAS B1938+666, exhibiting an unusually dense inner region embedded within an extended envelope, far exceeding expectations for cold dark matter (CDM) halos. Using gravothermal fluid simulations, we show that such a structure arises naturally in self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halos evolving into a deep core-collapse phase, where a secondary dense central core forms within an extended profile. The resulting density structure closely matches the inferred properties of the lensing object. We also demonstrate that a similar profile could be reproduced in CDM in the presence of an intermediate-mass black hole, but this requires an early-forming progenitor that subsequently loses $5$ orders of magnitude in mass through tidal stripping by the lens galaxy. Whether such a scenario can be realized in realistic cosmological environments remains an open question.

AI.tldr: A dense substructure in the strong-lensing system JVAS B1938+666, previously thought to be an unusual CDM halo, is naturally explained as a self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halo undergoing core collapse, forming a dense central core within an extended envelope. ACDM alternative requiring an intermediate-mass black hole and extreme tidal stripping is less plausible.
AI.motivation: To explain the anomalously dense inner region observed in the lensing object JVAS B1938+666, which cannot be accounted for by standard cold dark matter (CDM) halo profiles.
AI.method: Gravothermal fluid simulations of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halos evolving into a deep core-collapse phase, compared with an alternative CDM scenario involving an intermediate-mass black hole and tidal stripping.
AI.result: The SIDM core-collapse model produces a secondary dense central core within an extended profile that closely matches the inferred density structure of the lensing object. The CDM+black hole scenario can reproduce a similar profile but requires implausible fine-tuning: an early-forming progenitor that loses five orders of magnitude in mass via tidal stripping.
AI.conclusion: The observed dense substructure is naturally explained by SIDM halos undergoing core collapse, whereas the CDM-based alternative is unlikely in realistic cosmological environments.

title: Chemical signatures from the first stars embedded in metal-poor gas in galaxies at cosmic dawn
summary: The first generation of stars formed from pristine, neutral hydrogen gas. The most massive of these exploded as supernovae within a few million years of their birth, producing the first heavier elements and leaving distinct chemical signatures of their origin in the surrounding medium. However, chemical abundance studies have so far mainly relied on emission-line measurements, which are luminosity weighted and hence biased towards the most recently formed stars. Here we analyse near-infrared, medium-resolution spectroscopy from the JWST-SPURS program of three UV-bright galaxies at redshifts 7.8, 8.6, and 9.3, within the first 650 to 520 million years after the Big Bang. The chemical abundance patterns of the metal lines detected in absorption hint at extremely metal-poor gas, substantially lower than inferred from the emission lines tracing the central, star-forming regions. Further, they all exhibit super-solar [C/O] abundances, which is also imprinted in the averaged spectrum of a larger set of galaxies at similar redshifts. These results reveal the distinct chemical signatures of the first Population III supernovae explosions.

AI.tldr: JWST-SPURS program reveals chemical signatures of first Population III supernovae in three UV-bright galaxies at redshifts 7.8–9.3, showing extremely metal-poor gas with super-solar [C/O] abundances in absorption, contrasting with emission-line measurements.
AI.motivation: Chemical abundance studies of early galaxies have relied on emission-line measurements that are biased towards recently formed stars; absorption-line studies can reveal pristine chemical signatures from the first stars (Population III) that are otherwise masked.
AI.method: Near-infrared, medium-resolution spectroscopy from the JWST-SPURS program analyzing metal lines detected in absorption across three UV-bright galaxies at z=7.8, 8.6, and 9.3 (650–520 Myr after Big Bang).
AI.result: The absorption-line chemical abundances indicate extremely metal-poor gas, substantially lower than emission-line abundances; all three galaxies exhibit super-solar [C/O] ratios, which is also seen in the averaged spectrum of a larger galaxy sample at similar redshifts.
AI.conclusion: These absorption-line chemical signatures reveal the distinct imprints of the first Population III supernovae explosions in the early Universe.

title: Grain Alignment and Dust Evolution Physics with Polarisation (GRADE-POL). II. On the physical basis of Serkowski and super-Serkowski polarisation spectra
summary: Optical-to-near infrared interstellar polarisation, induced by aligned dust grains, generally follows a convex wavelength dependence, known as the Serkowski relation. However, observations in the ultraviolet (UV) and at [mid-]infrared wavelengths indicated that some of the spectra do not follow this relation. Specifically, about 25% show an excess in the degree of polarisation at mid-UV wavelengths ($λ^{-1} > 3\,\rm μm^{-1}$), referred to as the super-Serkowski polarisation. In this study, we re-examine both the Serkowski and super-Serkowski spectra based on the joint effect of paramagnetic relaxation (DG alignment) and radiative torque (RAT) alignment. We used the observational data for HD 30614, HD 204827, HD 37903 and HD 161056 to constrain our modelling. We examined two types of radiation fields: one derived from the scaled interstellar radiation field and another originating from a B-type star. For the super-Serkowski spectra of HD 30614 and HD 204827, our model demonstrates that RAT alignment enhanced by radiation produced from a B-type star below the Lyman limit ($λ=912 Å$) can reasonably explain the observations and that a combination with the DG alignments results in a better fit for $λ^{-1}\geq 5.5\,\rm μm^{-1}$. For the Serkowski spectra in HD 37903 and HD 161056, only RAT alignment by itself under the typical interstellar radiation field above the Lyman limit, within a typical cold neutral medium, can account for the observed spectra, with a combination of a very inefficient DG alignment. The capacity of our model to predict the starlight polarisation spectrum up to from infrared to far-UV is thus a promising tool for interpreting future missions that observe spectrophotometry in the UV bands.

AI.tldr: This study re-examines Serkowski and super-Serkowski interstellar polarisation spectra using paramagnetic relaxation (DG) and radiative torque (RAT) alignment models. Observations of four stars show that RAT alignment enhanced by B-type star radiation below the Lyman limit explains super-Serkowski spectra, while Serkowski spectra arise from RAT alignment alone in the standard interstellar radiation field.
AI.motivation: Approximately 25% of interstellar polarisation spectra exhibit a super-Serkowski excess in the mid-UV that deviates from the standard Serkowski relation. The physical origin of this excess remains unclear, motivating a re-examination using modern grain alignment theories.
AI.method: The authors model interstellar polarisation spectra by combining paramagnetic relaxation (DG alignment) and radiative torque (RAT) alignment mechanisms. They use observational data from four stars (HD 30614, HD 204827, HD 37903, HD 161056) and test two radiation field scenarios: scaled interstellar radiation field and B-type star radiation.
AI.result: For super-Serkowski spectra (HD 30614, HD 204827), RAT alignment enhanced by B-type star radiation below the Lyman limit (912 Å) explains observations, with combined DG alignment improving fits at λ⁻¹ ≥ 5.5 μm⁻¹. For Serkowski spectra (HD 37903, HD 161056), RAT alignment alone under standard interstellar radiation above the Lyman limit in cold neutral medium suffices, requiring very inefficient DG alignment.
AI.conclusion: The joint DG+RAT alignment model can successfully reproduce both Serkowski and super-Serkowski polarisation spectra across infrared to far-UV wavelengths, offering a promising tool for interpreting future UV spectrophotometric missions.

title: Beyond the Fundamental Metallicity Relation: galaxy sizes encode the link between inflow and metallicity
comment: 25 pages, 23 figures. Resubmitted to MNRAS after moderate revisions
summary: Gas-phase chemical abundances are key observable consequences of galaxy evolution, being intrinsically tied to galaxy formation histories. Gas metallicity rises with increasing stellar mass ($\mathrm{M_*}$), forming the well-known mass-metallicity relation (MZR). MZR residuals have separately been shown to anti-correlate with star-formation rate (the ``fundamental'' metallicity relation), with gas mass and with optical size, but no single analysis has considered all trends together. We thus perform a combined analysis of all three trends, utilizing optical MaNGA integral field spectroscopy, HI-MaNGA gas masses, and MaNGA DynPop dynamical masses. We estimate inner gas masses for $\sim$1500 star-forming galaxies, finding this to be the most important parameter after $\mathrm{M_*}$ in predicting gas metallicities. We obtain equivalent results for stellar metallicities and gaseous N/O, suggesting that current inner gas masses are intrinsically linked to long-term chemical evolution histories. We show that more compact galaxies have lower dynamical masses, challenging suggestions that deeper gravitational potentials confer higher metallicities. We find a strong correlation between inner gas mass and galaxy size, meaning that short term inflow fluctuations cannot be responsible for the MZR residuals. With chemical evolution models, we show that our results can instead be explained by differences in long-term inflow histories. The earlier inflow histories of compact galaxies lead to lower gas masses and more rapidly declining gas reservoirs at late times, leading to higher metallicities. At fixed stellar mass, galaxy size therefore encodes the link between halo assembly histories, long-term gas inflow histories, current gas reservoirs and metallicity.

AI.tldr: Using MaNGA and HI-MaNGA data for ~1500 star-forming galaxies, the study finds inner gas mass is the key secondary parameter (after stellar mass) driving the mass-metallicity relation residuals, and compact galaxies have higher metallicities due to earlier inflow histories and faster gas depletion, not deeper potentials.
AI.motivation: Individual studies have shown MZR residuals anti-correlate with SFR, gas mass, and optical size separately, but no combined analysis has been performed to understand which parameter is most fundamental and how these trends are physically connected.
AI.method: Combined analysis of optical MaNGA IFU spectroscopy, HI-MaNGA gas masses, and MaNGA DynPop dynamical masses for ~1500 star-forming galaxies; inner gas masses estimated; chemical evolution models used for interpretation.
AI.result: Inner gas mass is the most important parameter after M* for predicting gas metallicities. Compact galaxies have lower dynamical masses (challenging deeper potential theory). Strong correlation found between inner gas mass and galaxy size. Results consistent for stellar metallicities and N/O.
AI.conclusion: MZR residuals are explained by long-term inflow histories rather than short-term inflow fluctuations or deeper gravitational potentials. Galaxy size encodes the link between halo assembly, gas inflow histories, current gas reservoirs, and metallicity at fixed stellar mass.

title: Basis sets and Coulomb resolutions in rotational coordinates
comment: Author-accepted manuscript; see J. Phys. A for final published version
summary: Using generalised Laplacian symmetry operators, we construct basis sets or Coulomb resolutions in several separable coordinate systems, including two R-separable systems. This expands the possible geometries in which basis set construction is feasible, a problem which is relevant to both galactic dynamics and computational chemistry. In particular we derive three basis sets (two in prolate spheroidal and one in cylindrical coordinates) which are expressible in closed-form using a single Jacobi polynomial. We also show how any spherical polar or prolate spheroidal basis set may be transformed into a bispherical or toroidal basis set.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs basis sets (Coulomb resolutions) in multiple separable coordinate systems using generalized Laplacian symmetry operators, deriving three closed-form basis sets using Jacobi polynomials and showing transformations between coordinate systems.
AI.motivation: To expand the geometries in which basis set construction is feasible, benefiting galactic dynamics and computational chemistry.
AI.method: Using generalized Laplacian symmetry operators to construct basis sets in separable coordinate systems, including prolate spheroidal, cylindrical, bispherical, and toroidal coordinates.
AI.result: Three new basis sets (two in prolate spheroidal, one in cylindrical coordinates) expressed in closed-form using a single Jacobi polynomial. Transformations from spherical/prolate spheroidal to bispherical/toroidal basis sets are shown.
AI.conclusion: The work expands the range of coordinate systems where basis set construction is possible, with applications in both galactic dynamics and computational chemistry.

title: Galaxy clusters in the VIDEO fields: detection and characterisation in the context of MOONRISE
summary: We analyse the cluster content of the $\sim 4.5 \text{ deg}^{2}$ XMM-LSS and CDFS VIDEO fields which are expected to be partially covered by the upcoming MOONRISE survey. Using AMICO and WaZP photometric redshift-based cluster finders, we construct a sample of $519$ cluster candidates detected by both finders in the redshift range $z = 0.1-3$, including $74$ detections at $z > 1.5$. For all detections, we identify the Brightest Central Galaxy (BCG) and compute a list of probabilistic cluster memberships. Our photometric redshift measurements of the clusters agree well with spectroscopic redshifts from the literature, when available. From ancillary spectroscopic data, we assign $z_\text{spec}$ measurements to $116$ cluster candidates based on their spectroscopic members and to $204$ based on their likely BCGs. We also show that candidates containing Radio-Loud members are efficiently recovered using the prior-based cluster finder PPM. We perform a preliminary analysis of the galaxy content of these candidates, focusing on the Red-Sequence components of their apparent Colour-Magnitude Diagram. By comparing with models of galaxy evolution, we show that this population is consistent with a model of passive evolution with a formation at high redshift, and is already in place at $z = 1.5-2.0$. Finally, our cluster sample is used to evaluate how these clusters would be detected and characterised, according to various MOONRISE strategies. We show that cluster spectroscopic confirmation and characterisation could be efficiently achieved up to $z\sim1.7$ even with the shallowest survey strategy. This open unprecedented insight into the physical properties of high-redshift galaxy clusters and into galaxy formation in dense environments.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes ~519 galaxy cluster candidates (up to z=3) in the XMM-LSS and CDFS VIDEO fields from photometric redshift cluster finders, validates them with spectroscopic data, studies their red-sequence galaxy populations consistent with passive evolution since high redshift, and forecasts their detectability with the upcoming MOONRISE survey up to z~1.7.
AI.motivation: To construct and characterize a large sample of high-redshift galaxy cluster candidates in fields partially covered by the upcoming MOONRISE survey, and to evaluate how future survey strategies will enable cluster confirmation and studies of galaxy formation in dense environments.
AI.method: Used two photometric redshift-based cluster finders (AMICO and WaZP) on ~4.5 deg² of XMM-LSS and CDFS VIDEO fields; identified BCGs, computed probabilistic memberships; cross-matched with spectroscopic data; applied PPM prior-based finder for radio-loud members; analyzed Colour-Magnitude Diagrams with galaxy evolution models; simulated MOONRISE survey strategies.
AI.result: 519 common cluster candidates (74 at z>1.5); 116 and 204 candidates with spectroscopic member/BCG redshifts; efficient recovery of radio-loud members via PPM; red-sequence population consistent with passive evolution since high redshift, already in place at z=1.5-2.0; cluster confirmation feasible up to z~1.7 even with the shallowest MOONRISE strategy.
AI.conclusion: The sample provides unprecedented insight into high-redshift clusters and dense-environment galaxy formation, and demonstrates that MOONRISE can efficiently characterize clusters up to z~1.7.

title: Feedback in Extragalactic Star Clusters (FEAST): Spectral Energy Distributions and the Physical Properties of Star Clusters in NGC 628 with CIGALE
summary: With Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations of NGC~628 spanning 0.3--7.7\,$μ$m, we fit the spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of over 12,000 optically-selected star clusters, emerging young star clusters (eYSCs), and MIRI-selected sources with \textsc{cigale} to derive their ages, masses, extinctions, and dust properties. We find that near-infrared selected eYSC-I (compact Pa$α$ and 3.3,$μ$m PAH emission) and eYSC-II (compact Pa$α$ and diffuse 3.3,$μ$m PAH emssion) sources peak at $\sim$3--5~Myr, where $\sim 12\%$ of the clusters have an $E(B{-}V)>2$, demonstrating the presence of dust-embedded populations as clusters emerge. Further, the distributions of the fractional polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) abundance ($q_{\mathrm PAH}$) and stellar-to-nebular attenuation ratio ($E(B{-}V)_{\rm \star}/E(B{-}V)_{\rm neb}$) suggest an evolutionary sequence in which sources evolve from eYSC-I to eYSC-II as clusters clear their surrounding dust and gas. The photo-dissociation region (PDR) clearing timescale inferred from the ratio of eYSC-I to optically visible stellar clusters is $\sim$4~Myr. Additionally, we find that star clusters in the spiral arms of NGC 628 are preferentially more massive and more dust-reddened than those in inter-arm regions.~Finally, we find that $\sim$65\% of eYSC-I, $\sim$27\% of eYSC-II, and $\sim$40\% of F335M-selected sources coincide with an F770W peak in our MIRI-selected catalog within 4 pixels, confirming that F770W-bright sources preferentially trace the youngest and dustiest regions. Overall, our results highlight the ability of JWST together with \textsc{cigale} model grids to identify and characterize eYSCs during their short-lived embedded phases, and provide constraints on the feedback mechanisms that govern the emergence of stellar clusters.

AI.tldr: Using HST and JWST observations of NGC 628 (0.3–7.7 μm), this study fits SEDs for ~12,000 star clusters and emerging young star clusters (eYSCs) with CIGALE, finding that eYSCs peak at ~3–5 Myr, ~12% have E(B−V)>2, and an evolutionary sequence from eYSC-I to eYSC-II as clusters clear dust/gas. PDR clearing timescale is ~4 Myr, spiral arm clusters are more massive/dust-reddened, and ~65% of eYSC-I coincide with F770W peaks, highlighting JWST's capability to characterize embedded cluster phases.
AI.motivation: To understand how young star clusters emerge from their natal dust/gas envelopes by characterizing their ages, masses, extinction, and dust properties across evolutionary stages using combined HST and JWST multi-wavelength data.
AI.method: SED fitting of ~12,000 optically-selected star clusters, eYSCs (eYSC-I and eYSC-II), and MIRI-selected sources in NGC 628 across 0.3–7.7 μm using CIGALE to derive ages, masses, extinctions, and dust properties, supplemented by spatial correlation analysis with F770W peaks.
AI.result: eYSC-I and eYSC-II peak at ~3–5 Myr; ~12% have E(B−V)>2. qPAH and E(B−V)★/E(B−V)neb distributions indicate an evolutionary sequence from eYSC-I to eYSC-II. PDR clearing timescale ~4 Myr. Spiral arm clusters are more massive and dust-reddened. ~65% of eYSC-I, ~27% of eYSC-II, ~40% of F335M sources coincide with F770W peaks.
AI.conclusion: JWST combined with CIGALE model grids effectively identifies and characterizes embedded young star clusters, providing constraints on feedback mechanisms (e.g., PDR clearing) that govern cluster emergence and evolution.

title: Direct detection of cool molecular gas in a star-forming galaxy at $z=7.31$
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. Main text: 17 pages, 6 figures
summary: We investigate the molecular gas content and interstellar medium (ISM) conditions of REBELS-25, a massive, star-forming galaxy at $z=7.31$. Deep VLA Q-band and ALMA Band 3 observations reveal CO(3-2) and CO(7-6) emission (both at $\sim3.5σ$), and provide an upper limit on [C I](2-1). From the CMB-corrected CO(3-2) flux-representing the highest-redshift detection of a low-$J$ CO transition to date-we derive a molecular gas mass of $M_{\rm mol}=(1.0\pm0.4)\times10^{11}\,(α_{\rm CO}/(3\,$M$_{\odot}$(K$\,$\kms$\,$pc$^2)^{-1}))\,$M$_{\odot}$, directly confirming the presence of a very massive gas reservoir only $\simeq700\,$Myr after the Big Bang. This implies an extreme gas fraction of $f_{\rm gas}\simeq0.95$, a gas-to-dust ratio of $δ_{\rm GDR}\simeq6\times10^2$, and a depletion timescale of $τ_{\rm dep}\simeq1.2\,$Gyr, broadly consistent with extrapolated scaling relations for main-sequence galaxies at lower redshift. Using the radiative transfer code TUNER, we self-consistently model CO and dust continuum emission in the context of the significant CMB background, constraining ISM properties and recovering $M_{\rm mol}= (1.8^{+1.0}_{-0.9})\times10^{11}\,$M$_{\odot}$, independent of assumptions about $r_{31}$ and $α_{\rm CO}$. We further discuss the use of alternative molecular gas tracers at early epochs. Combining CO and [C II] measurements, we infer an empirical [C II]-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $α_{\rm [C II]}=(60\pm25)\,$M$_{\odot}$/L$_{\odot}$, suggesting [C II] remains a viable molecular gas tracer in the Epoch of Reionization. These results demonstrate the detectability of low-$J$ CO emission even at $z>7$, paving the way for next-generation facilities, and provide critical insights into the rapid mass assembly of galaxies during the first billion years of cosmic history.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the detection of CO(3-2) and CO(7-6) emission in REBELS-25 at z=7.31, confirming a massive gas reservoir (M_mol ~ 1-2×10¹¹ M☉) only ~700 Myr after the Big Bang, with extreme gas fraction (~0.95) and depletion timescale (~1.2 Gyr). Using radiative transfer modeling and multi-tracer analysis, it constrains ISM properties and validates [C II] as a molecular gas tracer in the Epoch of Reionization.
AI.motivation: To investigate molecular gas content and ISM conditions in REBELS-25, a massive star-forming galaxy at z=7.31, to understand gas assembly and star formation processes in the early Universe.
AI.method: VLA Q-band and ALMA Band 3 observations to detect CO(3-2) and CO(7-6); radiative transfer modeling with TUNER code to self-consistently model CO and dust continuum under CMB background; combined CO and [C II] analysis to derive empirical conversion factors.
AI.result: Detected CO(3-2) and CO(7-6) at ~3.5σ; derived M_mol=(1.0±0.4)×10¹¹ (α_CO/3) M☉ from CO(3-2); radiative transfer yields M_mol=(1.8⁺¹.⁰₋₀.₉)×10¹¹ M☉; gas fraction f_gas~0.95; gas-to-dust ratio δ_GDR~6×10²; depletion timescale τ_dep~1.2 Gyr; [C II]-to-H₂ conversion factor α_[C II]=(60±25) M☉/L☉.
AI.conclusion: Low-J CO emission is detectable at z>7, confirming massive gas reservoirs exist at early epochs; [C II] remains a viable molecular gas tracer during the Epoch of Reionization; results provide critical insights into rapid mass assembly of galaxies in the first billion years.

title: The ultra low-frequency spectral properties of bright extended radio galaxies in the 3CRR catalogue
summary: Context. Active galactic nuclei (AGN) jets are fundamental drivers of galaxy evolution, injecting kinetic energy into their environments. The large-scale morphology and spectral properties of these radio galaxies are consequences of complex particle acceleration, energy loss, and absorption processes. While the shape of the synchrotron spectrum encodes the plasma's energetic history, understanding the physics of particle acceleration and duty cycles has historically been limited by a lack of well-resolved observations at ultra-low frequencies (< 100 MHz), where the oldest cosmic ray electron populations are traced. Aims. This study aims to perform the first comprehensive multi-frequency analysis of bright extended radio galaxies down to 58 MHz. The goal is to study electron acceleration mechanisms, accurately measure the low-frequency spectral shape, and constrain the injection index for a sample of Fanaroff-Riley (FR) I and II galaxies using spectral ageing models. Methods. Utilising new 58 MHz observations from the LOFAR Low Band Antenna (LBA) combined with LOFAR High Band Antenna (HBA; 144 MHz) and Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS, 887 MHz & 943.5 MHz & 1367.5 MHz) data, a sub-sample of 22 extended sources from the 3CRR catalogue was selected, requiring the largest angular size to be at least 2.5'. The analysis involves constructing detailed spectral index maps and utilising radio colour-colour diagrams to interpret spectral shapes and constrain ageing model parameters across the radio lobes. Results. This study presents the ultra-low frequency spectral index maps for this sample. For FR I galaxies, spectral indices range from ~0.5 near the core (consistent with first-order Fermi acceleration) to > 1.0 in the lobes. For FR II galaxies, hotspots exhibit steep low-frequency spectra (0.5 - 0.9), suggesting complex acceleration or absorption effects.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first multi-frequency analysis of 22 bright extended radio galaxies down to 58 MHz using LOFAR LBA, LOFAR HBA, and RACS data. It constructs spectral index maps and radio colour-colour diagrams to study electron acceleration, measure low-frequency spectral shapes, and constrain injection indices for FR I and II galaxies using spectral ageing models. Key findings include spectral index variations from ~0.5 near FR I cores to >1.0 in lobes, and steep low-frequency spectra (0.5-0.9) in FR II hotspots.
AI.motivation: Understanding particle acceleration and duty cycles in AGN jets has been limited by a lack of well-resolved ultra-low frequency (< 100 MHz) observations, where the oldest cosmic ray electron populations are best traced. This study aims to fill this gap by performing comprehensive multi-frequency analysis down to 58 MHz.
AI.method: Selected 22 extended sources from the 3CRR catalogue with largest angular size ≥ 2.5'. Utilised new LOFAR LBA (58 MHz), LOFAR HBA (144 MHz), and RACS (887 MHz, 943.5 MHz, 1367.5 MHz) data. Constructed detailed spectral index maps and radio colour-colour diagrams to interpret spectral shapes and constrain spectral ageing model parameters across radio lobes.
AI.result: For FR I galaxies, spectral indices range from ~0.5 near the core (consistent with first-order Fermi acceleration) to >1.0 in the lobes. For FR II galaxies, hotspots exhibit steep low-frequency spectra (0.5-0.9), suggesting complex acceleration or absorption effects. Ultra-low frequency spectral index maps were produced for the sample.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates the power of ultra-low frequency observations for constraining electron acceleration mechanisms and spectral ageing models in radio galaxies, revealing distinct spectral behaviours between FR I and FR II populations.

title: Centrally concentrated star formation in young clusters II: Jet feedback
comment: Data products associated with this work will be made publicly available through the American Museum of Natural History Digital Library after the paper is accepted for publication
summary: Protostellar jets are one of the earliest forms of stellar feedback, but their impact on star formation and cluster assembly in centrally concentrated molecular clouds remains poorly understood. We study how protostellar jets affect the star formation efficiency, the temporal variability of star formation, star cluster structure, and the early dynamical state of centrally concentrated, newly forming star clusters using the Torch star cluster formation framework. We adopt a centrally concentrated initial cloud model with mass M = 2.5 x 10^3 solar masses and compare six pairs of simulations with and without protostellar jets, supplemented by one additional higher resolution pair of simulations. We analyze our simulations using global star formation diagnostics together with structural and dynamical measures of the stellar population. Models with jet feedback achieve star formation efficiencies of 12-16%, while the corresponding models without jets yield higher efficiencies of 19-33%. Jets also cause star formation to occur in discrete bursts rather than continuously, to produce more extended and substructured stellar systems, and to leave behind stellar populations that are less tightly bound and have higher virial parameters. In our centrally concentrated initial conditions, runs with jets form stellar systems that better reproduce the observed range of the projected structural parameter Q_2D in young clusters than runs without jets, indicating that protostellar jets are an important early feedback channel even in centrally concentrated clouds that regulates star formation efficiencies and shapes the emerging cluster structure.

AI.tldr: Protostellar jets reduce star formation efficiency (12-16% vs 19-33%), induce bursty star formation, create more extended/substructured stellar systems, and produce less bound populations with higher virial parameters in centrally concentrated clouds (M=2.5×10³ M☉). Jet-inclusive simulations better reproduce observed Q_2D structural parameters in young clusters.
AI.motivation: To understand how protostellar jets—as one of the earliest forms of stellar feedback—impact star formation efficiency, temporal variability, cluster structure, and dynamical state in centrally concentrated, newly forming star clusters, which remains poorly understood.
AI.method: Using the Torch star cluster formation framework, adopting a centrally concentrated initial cloud model (M = 2.5×10³ M☉), comparing six pairs of simulations with and without protostellar jets plus one higher-resolution pair, and analyzing global star formation diagnostics alongside structural/dynamical measures of the stellar population.
AI.result: Models with jets: SFE 12-16%; without jets: SFE 19-33%. Jets produce discrete bursty star formation, more extended/substructured systems, less bound populations, higher virial parameters, and better reproduce observed Q_2D values in young clusters.
AI.conclusion: Protostellar jets are an important early feedback channel even in centrally concentrated clouds, regulating star formation efficiencies and shaping emerging cluster structure.
